newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in late spurt on Telmex Q1 hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in late spurt on Telmex Q1 hopes.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed slightly higher Wednesday in a late upswing after zig-zagging through the session on a volatile Dow Jones and selective trading ahead of first quarter earnings reports.
"Trading was very, very selective and based on first quarter earnings expectations, so we decoupled from Wall Street today," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended up 11.48 points, or 0.30 percent, at 3,827.01.
Dealers said a record close in peso terms by telecommunications firm Telmex tipped the balance of a mixed bag of blue chips into positive turf at the close.
Telmex L shares closed up 10 centavos (1 cent) at a record 16.68 pesos ($2.12).
"Telmex is expected to report (first quarter earnings) tomorrow, and dealers see them in line with expectations, or good," another desk trader said.
Telmex ADRs meanwhile shrugged off a decline in the Dow Jones industrial average to gain strongly, up 5/8 at 42-1/2, but still below pre-devaluation record levels set in 1994.
The Dow closed down 20.87 points at 6,812.72.
Trading volume was brisker than on Monday and Tuesday at 99.6 million shares.
Financial group Bancomer weighed most on the downside, ending off six centavos (less than 1 cent) at 2.61 pesos (33 cents), but had pared losses from earlier lows.
Banacci, holding company for Mexico's largest bank Banamex, ended down 38 centavos (5 cents) at 16.42 pesos ($2.09).
Cement maker Cemex shares ended down on market forecasts of disappointing first quarter earnings.

Cemex CPO shares slid 65 centavos (8 cents) to 26.65 pesos ($3.39), the A shares fell 70 centavos (9 cents) to 26.80 pesos ($3.41) and the B class declined 55 centavos (7 cent s) to 29.80 pesos ($3.79).

Corn flour and tortilla maker Maseca swung wildly through the session, on speculative trade swayed by a changing outlook for tortilla prices. Maseca B shares ended up 12 centavos (less than 2 cents) at 7.86 pesos ($1.00).

Retail chain Cifra gained 36 centavos (5 cents) to 12.46 pesos ($1.48) on a combination of a favourable earnings outlook and news Wal-Mart Stores Inc. was in talks to acquire a possible equity interest in the company.
On the broad market, 110 stocks were traded of which gainers outnumbered decliners by 55 to 30.
